name: Nasaq
description: Independent Arabic-first UI components informed by DGA Platforms Code; no official endorsement or certification is claimed.

statusDefinitions.planned: An adapter is in scope; source may not exist yet.
statusDefinitions.built: Source exists for the named adapter; this does not establish complete verification.
statusDefinitions.verified: The named adapter has direct behavior, semantic-association, or layout-contract assertions recorded in evidence. Scope is limited to those cases; rendering-only and broad suite checks remain separate. This is not a blanket accessibility or DGA certification.

coverageNote: 77 entries: initial 27 plus 50 additions. Built records inspected source/export presence. Native/static vanilla entries use semantic HTML/CSS recipes; interactive entries also have exported controllers. The 22 native input types, variants, blocks, and specialist integration recipes are not extra components. Verified requires scoped passing evidence; rendering or source presence alone does not verify behavior. No release, accessibility, or DGA certification is implied.

limitations: Public source preview; npm packages are not published. No official DGA certification.
The 77-entry scope is finite and independently designed; exact parity with the current official DGA catalog has not been established.
Combobox is local and single-select. MultiSelect is a separate searchable checkbox list; async data and virtualization are application concerns.
DataTable provides stable localized sorting, not virtualization or cell editing.
FileUpload and FileDropzone select local files; application code owns transport, storage, and server validation.

Calendar/DatePicker use Gregorian ISO date-only values and Gregorian/Umm al-Qura display. Pinned reference data, supported range, and official-source limits are documented in docs/date-calendars.md. General Intl formatDate is not the canonical converter for persisted dual-calendar records.
Phone, IBAN, identity, and address recipes collect data; they do not verify identity, ownership, or government-service access.
Maps, charts, editors, PDF, CAPTCHA, authentication, and payments are integration recipes, not bundled engines or connected services.
Headless behavior is project-owned; there is no Zag dependency.
Angular builds as an APF library; the Vite JIT example does not establish production AOT, SSR, or hydration coverage.
Demo journeys use fictional data and simulated submission/request tracking.
